# Version Embedding Reference

What `glassfrog --version` and the `glassfrog version` command report across every way the CLI can be built or installed, and the precedence by which that value is resolved.

## Overview

The version a binary reports is resolved at runtime by a fixed three-tier precedence. A release build stamps the published tag into the binary at link time; when no version is stamped, the binary falls back to the module version Go recorded in its build info; when even that is unavailable, it reports a clear development placeholder. The reported value is **never empty** on any path.

Version Embedding changes only the *value* that `--version` and `version` report — it adds no new command or flag. The `--version` flag and the `version` command are owned and formatted elsewhere; both read the same resolved value, so their output is byte-identical. Version resolution requires no network or VCS access at runtime; both inputs are baked into the binary at build time.

## Reporting Surfaces

Two surfaces report the version, and they always agree:

- `glassfrog --version` — the version flag.
- `glassfrog version` — the version command.

Both print the single resolved value. Version resolution produces the value but does not decide how it is printed and does not add commit or date build metadata.

## Resolution Precedence

The version is resolved by the following precedence; the first match wins:

1. **Stamped (injected) version** — if a version was stamped into the binary at build time, that value is reported.
2. **Recorded module build info** — otherwise, if Go recorded a non-empty module version in the binary's build info, that value is reported **verbatim** (no trimming or normalization).
3. **Placeholder** — otherwise, the development placeholder `0.0.0-dev` is reported.

The placeholder is non-empty, semver-shaped, and clearly not a release.

## Reported Value by Build/Install Path

| Build / install path | Stamped version | Reported value |
|---|---|---|
| Release build (tag `v1.4.0`) | `v1.4.0` (injected) | `v1.4.0` |
| Release build, pre-release tag (`v1.4.0-rc.1`) | `v1.4.0-rc.1` (injected) | `v1.4.0-rc.1` (suffix preserved) |
| Snapshot build (local/CI) | `v…-next-<commit>` (injected) | the snapshot version |
| `go install …@v1.3.2` (tagged source) | none | `v1.3.2` (build info, verbatim) |
| `go install …@latest` (untagged) | none | `v0.0.0-<ts>-<commit>` pseudo-version (verbatim) |
| Plain `go build` | none | `(devel)` (build info, verbatim) |
| No build info at all | none | `0.0.0-dev` (placeholder) |

The value is never empty in any path.

### Notes on the build-info path

- A **tagged source install** (`go install path@v1.3.2`) reports the recorded tag verbatim, e.g. `v1.3.2`.
- An **untagged source install** reports the Go pseudo-version verbatim, e.g. `v0.0.0-20260101120000-abc123def456`, which identifies the exact commit.
- A **plain local build** reports Go's development marker `(devel)` verbatim.

`runtime/debug.ReadBuildInfo().Main.Version` is the source-build version: Go records the module version there for `go install path@version` (a real tag or a pseudo-version) and `(devel)` for a plain `go build` of the main module.

## Release Stamping

On a release build, the published tag is stamped into the version variable at link time, so a shipped binary self-reports its real version rather than the development placeholder. The stamped value carries the `vX.Y.Z` shape (for example `v1.4.0`), and a pre-release suffix is preserved exactly (`v1.4.0-rc.1`). Both the snapshot build and the tagged release build stamp a value; plain `go build` and `go install` apply no stamping, so the binary falls back to build info.

## Behavior and Error Conditions

Version resolution has no runtime error states — it always returns a non-empty string and never fails for lack of network or VCS access. The contract concerns misconfiguration being caught at build/test time rather than runtime errors.

| Condition | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Reported version is empty | Contract violation — the never-empty invariant; a resolver test fails. |
| Release stamping seam blanked / version not injected | A focused build-config assertion fails, reporting that the configuration no longer injects the version variable. (A blanked seam would silently degrade releases to the build-info or placeholder value.) |
| Stamping target stale (variable renamed, seam not updated) | The stamped value never lands; the binary falls back to build info or the placeholder. The same build-config assertion catches the stale target. |
| Stamped value drops the required `v` prefix | Contract violation — the build-config assertion rejects an injected value that does not begin with `v`. |
| Build info absent (unusual build mode) | Not an error — the designed placeholder path; reports `0.0.0-dev`. |
| `--version` and `version` disagree | Contract violation — both must read the same resolved value; a parity test fails. |

## Notes

- The placeholder literal `0.0.0-dev` is the recognizable non-release marker. The behavioral requirement is "non-empty and clearly not a release"; the exact literal is not a published knob.
